title: Revised Trauma Score (RTS)
sources: Champion HR et al. J Trauma 1989

changelog.change: Initial entry — from ED_ICU_OR_Calculators.xlsx. Triage RTS (coded-value sum, unweighted).

purpose: Physiologic trauma severity score from three coded parameters (GCS, systolic BP, respiratory rate), each 0–4. This is the Triage-RTS (T-RTS) — the simple unweighted sum used at the bedside / in the field. A T-RTS ≤ 11 identifies a patient who should be taken to a trauma centre.

interpretation.label: Extremely severe physiologic derangement — very high mortality. Maximal resuscitation, immediate trauma team, damage-control approach
Severe — trauma-centre care, trauma team activation, early imaging and definitive haemorrhage control
T-RTS 11 — triage threshold. Transport to / manage at a trauma centre; do not undertriage

T-RTS 12 — normal physiology at this snapshot. Does NOT exclude serious injury (normal vitals are common early in significant trauma) — full secondary survey, serial reassessment, imaging per mechanism

notes: The prognostic RTS uses weighted coefficients (0.9368·GCS_c + 0.7326·SBP_c + 0.2908·RR_c, range 0–7.84) and feeds the TRISS methodology for survival probability — that is a registry/audit tool, not a bedside one. Use T-RTS for triage only; it is a snapshot and must be repeated. Intubation/sedation invalidates the GCS and RR components.
buildNote: Triage-RTS: unweighted sum of three coded values, range 0–12. Prognostic weighted RTS noted in text.
